why: Commits 1 and 3 are written out and covered by int cases and a scan, but commit 2 ends with 'every further line the scan prints' in files the brief does not name, and for each catch the executor must judge whether it is an error or a normal state (stop_if 2); a cheap model that 'makes the scan pass' will add report() to a catch that handles 'not connected', marking that job failing on every run and sending the platform admins a failure alert every few turns. The edited entry functions include payHostCommissions, invoiceJobs, runBonusJobs and the refund-deadline reminders, where a slip in a .catch() return value changes what the job does next and the int tests may not reach that branch.
harm_if_wrong: A healthy money job (commissions, invoices, refunds) shows as failing and alerts every run, or a rewritten catch returns a different value and changes what the job does after a failure, with the scan and type check green.
make_it_cheaper: List every catch the scan will print today by file, line and part name, with a verdict for each (report, or leave because it is a normal state, as an explicit allow-list entry with its reason), so commit 2 has no open-ended 'and whatever else the scan names'.
brief_problems: The scan reads the dispatcher's job object from src/app/api/cron/cart-reminders/route.ts, but step 1.10 (earlier in the plan) moves it to src/server/dispatcher-jobs.ts as DISPATCHER_JOBS; the scan must resolve imports from that file, and the route edit in commit 2 must land there.

do_not 6 forbids an exempt list while stop_if 2 says some catches handle a normal state and must not report: the brief gives no way to make the scan pass for those, so the cheap model will either stop or report a normal state.

Commit 3's cron-health edit is written as a conditional; today cronHealth() computes lateness from everySeconds alone and the row carries its job name, so the brief can simply say to add the '.work is never late' rule.
